winged-zebrafish.desired_phenotype: a zebrafish with wings: enlarged pectoral fins that let it glide over the water like a flying fish

closest_functional_analogue.name: flying fishes
closest_functional_analogue.function: glides over water after leaving it
closest_functional_analogue.function_operational_definition: leaves the water and travels through air over a measurable distance without flapping-powered thrust. Satisfied by a taxon for which a glide distance or duration is reported, or for which the gliding habit is the taxon-defining behaviour in the primary literature.
closest_functional_analogue.function_signal: specified: parsed from the desired-phenotype text ("glide")
closest_functional_analogue.basis: satisfies the operational definition of "glides over water after leaving it"
closest_functional_analogue.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A (genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json); Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

evidence.claim: Exocoetidae are the gliding clade of the Beloniformes; Daane 2021 groups the family as the gliding end of a four-group series (needlefish -> halfbeak -> gliding halfbeak -> flying fish) and measures the fin proportion that supports the glide
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A (genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json)

evidence.claim: pectoral fin length / SL median 0.687 (range 0.406-0.823, n = 49 museum specimens)
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

phylogenetic.mrca_source: Ensembl Compara orthologue records fetched for the requirement loci (homology taxonomy_level); see C:/Temp/functional-cache/ortho/
phylogenetic.dated_divergence_note: NOT asserted: no source fetched in this thread dates the Otophysi-Acanthomorpha split, so no number is given rather than a remembered one

functional.why_unmeasurable: The design side has no number. design-validation/REPORT.md axis 1 is CANNOT SCORE on BOTH sides at once: no fetched source gives an adult zebrafish pectoral fin length / SL (development/zebrafish/trajectory.mjs returns finLength_SL: null), and the winged zebrafish's own value exists only inside Daane 2021 Figure 4B, which this project refuses to digitise. The single number that would settle the headline question is unavailable at both ends.

distance.rule: the two distances are reported separately and never combined: a close functional analogue may be phylogenetically remote, and that is the whole point of choosing by function

evidence.claim: an independent, shallower glider inside the same order: pectoral fin length / SL median 0.274 (range 0.175-0.388, n = 19)
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

evidence.claim: gliding halfbeaks carry about as many of the Exocoetidae-derived coding states as flying fishes do, at a fin ratio 2.5x smaller, so derived-state count does not scale with fin length
evidence.source: sequences/progression.json read_this_first[1] (our own re-read of Daane sheet G per species from the captured exons)

closest_functional_analogue.data_poor_statement: The ONLY analogue for this function has a genome and nothing else: no transcriptome, no proteome, no expression atlas, no mutant, no functional assay, and 9 of 3,860 genes carry an identifier for it. Every functional requirement derived from it is therefore derived from SEQUENCE and from the curated comparative analysis in one paper - never from a measurement of the analogue doing the thing.

functional_data_we_hold.genome: a draft genome and gene set exist for ONE flying fish, Hirundichthys speculiger (Xu et al. 2021, Front Genet 12:695700, doi 10.3389/fgene.2021.695700, assembly GCA_018398805.1)
functional_data_we_hold.transcriptome: NONE. omics/transcriptomic/SOURCES.md: no flying-fish RNA-seq, raw or processed, exists in SRA/ENA/GEO/ArrayExpress; 3,485 loose Europe PMC hits and not one flying-fish transcriptome. In particular NO pectoral-fin expression data
functional_data_we_hold.proteome: NONE. omics/proteomic/SOURCES.md: 3 UniProt rows for flying-fish entries in 199,149; no MS evidence, no abundance, no structures
functional_data_we_hold.focal_gene_ids: omics/genes.json coverage.flying_fish = 9 of 3,860 genes carry a Hirundichthys identifier; 7 of 9 are clean reciprocal best hits (genotype/sequence-layer.json counts)
functional_data_we_hold.mutants_or_assays: NONE. No flying fish has ever been mutated, knocked down or functionally assayed in any source we fetched

closest_functional_analogue.direction_detected_by: the base does not satisfy the function and the design is to gain it

direction_evidence.claim: no glide, leap or aerial behaviour is reported for Danio rerio in any source this project fetched, and its pectoral fin length / SL is NOT MEASURED IN ANY FETCHED SOURCE (genotype/compare-2x2.json panel A). So "the base lacks the function" rests on the absence of any report, which is weaker than a measurement and is labelled as such
direction_evidence.source: genotype/compare-2x2.json; sim-engine organism document zebrafish-adult (pectoral_len_over_SL kind "assumed")

base_genome.source: the design is the zebrafish reference plus 2 edited loci (sequences/engineered-diff.json: "Not a full genome. It is a short list of edits to the zebrafish reference (GRCz11)")

design.label: the "winged zebrafish": the germline double heterozygote Daane et al. 2021 built and described as phenocopying the flying-fish bauplan
design.genotype_source: sequences/engineered-diff.json winged_zebrafish (from genotype/compare-2x2.json panel B and genotype/interventions.json kcnh2a-lof-x-lat4a-nr21-double-het)

edits.source: sequences/engineered-diff.json winged_zebrafish.protein_effects[0]; Daane et al. 2021, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441

edits.edit: cis-regulatory inversion placing prrx1a regulatory sequence upstream of kcnh2a
edits.source: sequences/engineered-diff.json winged_zebrafish.kinds[1]; Daane et al. 2021, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441; genotype/interventions.json

design.not_ours: the design is NOT ours: Daane et al. 2021, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441 built this animal. design-validation/REPORT.md states this plainly, and it bears on every claim made about it here.

ledger.requirement: the analogue carries the Exocoetidae-associated derived residue L in place of F at position 326 of lat4a (ENSORLG00000009715)
ledger.hypothesis_why: ALLELIC is sound as "this difference is an allele that occurs in a real organism" and UNSOUND as "this difference is functionally neutral" (validate/functional-interface.mjs). No experiment in our sources shows that p.T200K produces the same functional state as F326L, so the resolution is hypothesised. design-validation/REPORT.md records the same fact as a pre-registered result: the design "does not reproduce the flying fish's substitution; it changes a different position in the same transporter".

coverage.note: we can assess 22 of 73 requirements; the rest are unassessable, each with its own stated reason. ZERO of the loci have flying-fish expression or functional-assay data of any kind, because no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or assay exists in any archive we searched. Every "requirement" is therefore a SEQUENCE STATE in the analogue, never a measured function of the analogue.

It is not a causal set and not a complete one.

source_dataset.what_this_is: Every locus Daane 2021 reports as DIFFERING in flying fishes, turned into a requirement on a design. Sheet G is a per-site state requirement (a residue). Sheet I is a per-gene RATE requirement and has no state, so nothing a design does can be compared against it; it is kept because leaving it out would flatter the coverage number.
what_this_is_not: NOT the set of loci that differ in flying fishes. It is the set KNOWN to differ: 74 coding loci against the 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes of the Hirundichthys speculiger assembly (0.31 %).

NOT a causal set. Daane 2021 reports convergent substitutions and rate shifts; our own sequences/progression.json warns that tracking is not causing, and that the non-gliders score zero at these sites BY CONSTRUCTION.

NOT a non-coding requirement set. Sheets K and M (accelerated conserved non-coding elements) are GO-term enrichment tables with no gene column, so the regulatory requirements - which is where most between-species difference lives - cannot be enumerated at all. That is a named gap, not a zero.

ledger.requirement_set_scope: The requirement set is the set of loci Daane 2021 reports as KNOWN to differ in flying fishes (74 coding loci against 23,611 predicted genes = 0.31 % of the gene set), plus nothing for the regulatory changes, which cannot be enumerated because the accelerated-CNE sheets give GO terms and no gene names. It is not a causal set and not a complete one.

source_dataset.what_this_is: Every locus Daane 2021 reports as DIFFERING in flying fishes, turned into a requirement on a design. Sheet G is a per-site state requirement (a residue). Sheet I is a per-gene RATE requirement and has no state, so nothing a design does can be compared against it; it is kept because leaving it out would flatter the coverage number.
what_this_is_not: NOT the set of loci that differ in flying fishes. It is the set KNOWN to differ: 74 coding loci against the 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes of the Hirundichthys speculiger assembly (0.31 %).

NOT a causal set. Daane 2021 reports convergent substitutions and rate shifts; our own sequences/progression.json warns that tracking is not causing, and that the non-gliders score zero at these sites BY CONSTRUCTION.

NOT a non-coding requirement set. Sheets K and M (accelerated conserved non-coding elements) are GO-term enrichment tables with no gene column, so the regulatory requirements - which is where most between-species difference lives - cannot be enumerated at all. That is a named gap, not a zero.

compensation_rule.scoring_rule: a requirement is MET by compensation only on class "documented" AND functional_rescue === true; "plausible-by-rule" is an UNMET requirement with a review flag; "not-expected" is trusted; "unknown" is never a pass

ledger.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout).

closest_functional_analogue.data_poor_statement: The ONLY analogue for this function has a genome and nothing else: no transcriptome, no proteome, no expression atlas, no mutant, no functional assay, and 9 of 3,860 genes carry an identifier for it. coverage.note: we can assess 22 of 73 requirements; the rest are unassessable, each with its own stated reason. ZERO of the loci have flying-fish expression or functional-assay data of any kind, because no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or assay exists in any archive we searched. Every "requirement" is therefore a SEQUENCE STATE in the analogue, never a measured function of the analogue.

ledger.requirement_set_scope: The requirement set is the set of loci Daane 2021 reports as KNOWN to differ in flying fishes (74 coding loci against 23,611 predicted genes = 0.31 % of the gene set), plus nothing for the regulatory changes, which cannot be enumerated because the accelerated-CNE sheets give GO terms and no gene names. It is not a causal set and not a complete one.

source_dataset.what_this_is: Every locus Daane 2021 reports as DIFFERING in flying fishes, turned into a requirement on a design. Sheet G is a per-site state requirement (a residue). Sheet I is a per-gene RATE requirement and has no state, so nothing a design does can be compared against it; it is kept because leaving it out would flatter the coverage number.
what_this_is_not: NOT the set of loci that differ in flying fishes. It is the set KNOWN to differ: 74 coding loci against the 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes of the Hirundichthys speculiger assembly (0.31 %).

NOT a causal set. Daane 2021 reports convergent substitutions and rate shifts; our own sequences/progression.json warns that tracking is not causing, and that the non-gliders score zero at these sites BY CONSTRUCTION.

NOT a non-coding requirement set. Sheets K and M (accelerated conserved non-coding elements) are GO-term enrichment tables with no gene column, so the regulatory requirements - which is where most between-species difference lives - cannot be enumerated at all. That is a named gap, not a zero.

compensation_rule.scoring_rule: a requirement is MET by compensation only on class "documented" AND functional_rescue === true; "plausible-by-rule" is an UNMET requirement with a review flag; "not-expected" is trusted; "unknown" is never a pass

ledger.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout).

ledger.headline: We can assess 22 of 73 requirements (30.1 %); the other 51 are unassessable, each with a stated reason. Of the 22 assessable differences: 22 have a DEMONSTRATED resolution, 0 rest on a HYPOTHESIS, and 0 are UNRESOLVED. ZERO loci have any flying-fish expression or functional-assay data.

resolution_two_ways.rule: the two fractions are reported separately and are NEVER summed. "Could be compensated" is a hypothesis, not evidence.

coverage.note: we can assess 22 of 73 requirements; the rest are unassessable, each with its own stated reason. ZERO of the loci have flying-fish expression or functional-assay data of any kind, because no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or assay exists in any archive we searched. Every "requirement" is therefore a SEQUENCE STATE in the analogue, never a measured function of the analogue.

ledger.requirement_set_scope: The requirement set is the set of loci Daane 2021 reports as KNOWN to differ in flying fishes (74 coding loci against 23,611 predicted genes = 0.31 % of the gene set), plus nothing for the regulatory changes, which cannot be enumerated because the accelerated-CNE sheets give GO terms and no gene names. It is not a causal set and not a complete one.

sources.gene_universe: omics/genes.json (3,860 zebrafish genes; join key zfin_id)

source_dataset.what_this_is: Every locus Daane 2021 reports as DIFFERING in flying fishes, turned into a requirement on a design. Sheet G is a per-site state requirement (a residue). Sheet I is a per-gene RATE requirement and has no state, so nothing a design does can be compared against it; it is kept because leaving it out would flatter the coverage number.
what_this_is_not: NOT the set of loci that differ in flying fishes. It is the set KNOWN to differ: 74 coding loci against the 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes of the Hirundichthys speculiger assembly (0.31 %).

NOT a causal set. Daane 2021 reports convergent substitutions and rate shifts; our own sequences/progression.json warns that tracking is not causing, and that the non-gliders score zero at these sites BY CONSTRUCTION.

NOT a non-coding requirement set. Sheets K and M (accelerated conserved non-coding elements) are GO-term enrichment tables with no gene column, so the regulatory requirements - which is where most between-species difference lives - cannot be enumerated at all. That is a named gap, not a zero.

compensation_rule.scoring_rule: a requirement is MET by compensation only on class "documented" AND functional_rescue === true; "plausible-by-rule" is an UNMET requirement with a review flag; "not-expected" is trusted; "unknown" is never a pass

ledger.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout).

desired_phenotype.text: glides over the water like a flying fish

resolution.note: demonstrated and hypothesised are never summed; "could be compensated" is not a resolution

as_the_scorer_sees_it.gate: every difference has a demonstrated resolution

wingless-flying-fish.desired_phenotype: a flying fish with ordinary fins that no longer glides

closest_functional_analogue.name: flying fishes
closest_functional_analogue.function: glides over water after leaving it
closest_functional_analogue.function_operational_definition: leaves the water and travels through air over a measurable distance without flapping-powered thrust. Satisfied by a taxon for which a glide distance or duration is reported, or for which the gliding habit is the taxon-defining behaviour in the primary literature.
closest_functional_analogue.function_signal: specified: parsed from the desired-phenotype text ("flying fish")
closest_functional_analogue.basis: satisfies the operational definition of "glides over water after leaving it"
closest_functional_analogue.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A (genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json); Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

evidence.claim: Exocoetidae are the gliding clade of the Beloniformes; Daane 2021 groups the family as the gliding end of a four-group series (needlefish -> halfbeak -> gliding halfbeak -> flying fish) and measures the fin proportion that supports the glide
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A (genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json)

evidence.claim: pectoral fin length / SL median 0.687 (range 0.406-0.823, n = 49 museum specimens)
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

phylogenetic.dated_divergence_note: NOT asserted: no source fetched in this thread dates the Otophysi-Acanthomorpha split, so no number is given rather than a remembered one

functional.why_unmeasurable: The design side has no number. design-validation/REPORT.md axis 1 is CANNOT SCORE on BOTH sides at once: no fetched source gives an adult zebrafish pectoral fin length / SL (development/zebrafish/trajectory.mjs returns finLength_SL: null), and the winged zebrafish's own value exists only inside Daane 2021 Figure 4B, which this project refuses to digitise. The single number that would settle the headline question is unavailable at both ends.

distance.rule: the two distances are reported separately and never combined: a close functional analogue may be phylogenetically remote, and that is the whole point of choosing by function

evidence.claim: an independent, shallower glider inside the same order: pectoral fin length / SL median 0.274 (range 0.175-0.388, n = 19)
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

evidence.claim: gliding halfbeaks carry about as many of the Exocoetidae-derived coding states as flying fishes do, at a fin ratio 2.5x smaller, so derived-state count does not scale with fin length
evidence.source: sequences/progression.json read_this_first[1] (our own re-read of Daane sheet G per species from the captured exons)

closest_functional_analogue.data_poor_statement: The ONLY analogue for this function has a genome and nothing else: no transcriptome, no proteome, no expression atlas, no mutant, no functional assay, and 9 of 3,860 genes carry an identifier for it. Every functional requirement derived from it is therefore derived from SEQUENCE and from the curated comparative analysis in one paper - never from a measurement of the analogue doing the thing.

functional_data_we_hold.genome: a draft genome and gene set exist for ONE flying fish, Hirundichthys speculiger (Xu et al. 2021, Front Genet 12:695700, doi 10.3389/fgene.2021.695700, assembly GCA_018398805.1)
functional_data_we_hold.transcriptome: NONE. omics/transcriptomic/SOURCES.md: no flying-fish RNA-seq, raw or processed, exists in SRA/ENA/GEO/ArrayExpress; 3,485 loose Europe PMC hits and not one flying-fish transcriptome. In particular NO pectoral-fin expression data
functional_data_we_hold.proteome: NONE. omics/proteomic/SOURCES.md: 3 UniProt rows for flying-fish entries in 199,149; no MS evidence, no abundance, no structures
functional_data_we_hold.focal_gene_ids: omics/genes.json coverage.flying_fish = 9 of 3,860 genes carry a Hirundichthys identifier; 7 of 9 are clean reciprocal best hits (genotype/sequence-layer.json counts)
functional_data_we_hold.mutants_or_assays: NONE. No flying fish has ever been mutated, knocked down or functionally assayed in any source we fetched

closest_functional_analogue.direction_detected_by: the design is a recorded subtraction (its base satisfies the function and its parameters put it at the non-performing value)

direction_evidence.claim: the base (Hirundichthys / Exocoetidae) satisfies "glides over water after leaving it"
the design document puts pectoral_len_over_SL at the halfbeak group median 0.140 on a flying fish's body

base_genome.source: sim-engine organism document: parent flying-fish at weight 1

design.label: wingless flying fish - a real flying fish with the pectoral fin proportion put at the halfbeak value (0.140)
design.genotype_source: sim-engine organism document: parent flying-fish, pectoral_len_over_SL 0.14 (halfbeak group median, Daane sheet A), kind "hypothetical"
design.no_genotype_note: A SUBTRACTION design with no genotype: the function is removed by changing one shape parameter, not by changing a locus. Its genome is the flying fish's.

requirement_set.requirement: an organism that lacks gliding carries the ancestral residue F at position 326 of lat4a; the design, descended from a glider, carries the derived L unless it reverted it
requirement_set.source: Daane et al. 2021, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 (genotype/cache/daane2021_data_s1_mmc2.xlsx), sheet G; the per-species residue re-read from the captured exons (sequences/scripts/fetch_sheetG.py)
requirement_set.unassessable_reason: UNASSESSABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. Daane 2021 sheet G lists only substitutions that are shared by gliders and ABSENT from the outgroups, so every non-gliding species carries the ancestral residue at these sites BY DEFINITION (sequences/progression.json read_this_first[1] says exactly this: "THE NON-GLIDERS SCORE ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION ... the zero is circular and is not a finding"). A locus set built that way carries no information about whether a glider genotype is compatible with a non-gliding body, which is the only question a subtraction asks. Our own data says more: the gliding halfbeaks carry about as many derived states as the flying fishes at a fin ratio 2.5x smaller, so derived-state count does not track the function even among gliders.
requirement_set.analogue_has: L in undefined/undefined Exocoetidae species with data

requirement_set.unassessable_reason: UNASSESSABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. Daane 2021 sheet G lists only substitutions that are shared by gliders and ABSENT from the outgroups, so every non-gliding species carries the ancestral residue at these sites BY DEFINITION (sequences/progression.json read_this_first[1] says exactly this: "THE NON-GLIDERS SCORE ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION ... the zero is circular and is not a finding"). A locus set built that way carries no information about whether a glider genotype is compatible with a non-gliding body, which is the only question a subtraction asks. Our own data says more: the gliding halfbeaks carry about as many derived states as the flying fishes at a fin ratio 2.5x smaller, so derived-state count does not track the function even among gliders.

Daane 2021 sheet G lists only substitutions that are shared by gliders and ABSENT from the outgroups, so every non-gliding species carries the ancestral residue at these sites BY DEFINITION (sequences/progression.json read_this_first[1] says exactly this: "THE NON-GLIDERS SCORE ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION ... the zero is circular and is not a finding"). A locus set built that way carries no information about whether a glider genotype is compatible with a non-gliding body, which is the only question a subtraction asks. Our own data says more: the gliding halfbeaks carry about as many derived states as the flying fishes at a fin ratio 2.5x smaller, so derived-state count does not track the function even among gliders.

ledger.headline: SUBTRACTION. 41 requirements were derived against an organism that already lacks the function, and 0 of them are assessable. A subtraction is a different animal, not a pile of unmet requirements, and this ledger does not score it as one.

resolution_two_ways.rule: the two fractions are reported separately and are NEVER summed. "Could be compensated" is a hypothesis, not evidence.

coverage.note: we can assess 0 of 41 requirements; the rest are unassessable, each with its own stated reason. ZERO of the loci have flying-fish expression or functional-assay data of any kind, because no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or assay exists in any archive we searched. Every "requirement" is therefore a SEQUENCE STATE in the analogue, never a measured function of the analogue.

ledger.requirement_set_scope: The requirement set is the set of loci Daane 2021 reports as KNOWN to differ in flying fishes (74 coding loci against 23,611 predicted genes = 0.31 % of the gene set), plus nothing for the regulatory changes, which cannot be enumerated because the accelerated-CNE sheets give GO terms and no gene names. It is not a causal set and not a complete one.

source_dataset.what_this_is: Every locus Daane 2021 reports as DIFFERING in flying fishes, turned into a requirement on a design. Sheet G is a per-site state requirement (a residue). Sheet I is a per-gene RATE requirement and has no state, so nothing a design does can be compared against it; it is kept because leaving it out would flatter the coverage number.
what_this_is_not: NOT the set of loci that differ in flying fishes. It is the set KNOWN to differ: 74 coding loci against the 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes of the Hirundichthys speculiger assembly (0.31 %).

NOT a causal set. Daane 2021 reports convergent substitutions and rate shifts; our own sequences/progression.json warns that tracking is not causing, and that the non-gliders score zero at these sites BY CONSTRUCTION.

NOT a non-coding requirement set. Sheets K and M (accelerated conserved non-coding elements) are GO-term enrichment tables with no gene column, so the regulatory requirements - which is where most between-species difference lives - cannot be enumerated at all. That is a named gap, not a zero.

compensation_rule.scoring_rule: a requirement is MET by compensation only on class "documented" AND functional_rescue === true; "plausible-by-rule" is an UNMET requirement with a review flag; "not-expected" is trusted; "unknown" is never a pass

ledger.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout).

resolution.note: demonstrated and hypothesised are never summed; "could be compensated" is not a resolution
